shots.say: What do camels eat in the desert?
Grass? Leaves? Or prickly thorns?
I'm Milo. Let's find out with Sandy!
Welcome to The Animated Zoo, friends!
Today we fly to the sandy desert, for lunch!
Here we are! It is hot and dry. Only a few plants grow here.
This is Sandy, the baby camel. Sandy is hungry!
Camels eat plants that grow in the desert.
Grass, leaves, and little twigs. Yum!
Say it with me. Grass, leaves, and twigs!
Let's count them. One, two, three!
Sandy looks, and looks. Camels are very clever at finding food.
Sandy finds some grass. Munch, munch!
Then Sandy and Mama walk to a little bush.
Sandy nibbles the green leaves. Nibble, nibble!
Does a camel eat leaves, or rocks?
Leaves! Camels eat leaves, and grass, and twigs.
Can you nibble like a camel? Nibble, nibble!
Look! Sandy eats only a few leaves.
Count the leaves she eats. One, two, three!
Then she walks on, to the next plant.
Camels take just a few leaves from each plant.
Does a camel eat all the leaves, or just a few?
Camels spend their days eating. Munch, munch, all day long!
From the morning, until the sun goes down!
What do you like to eat for lunch?
Rub your tummy. Mmm, yum!
Point to the leaf! Where is the leaf?
Grass, leaves, and twigs. A camel's lunch!
Look at this bush. It is covered in thorns!
Thorns are hard and pointy. Many animals cannot eat them.
Can a camel eat thorny plants? Yes, or no?
Yes! Mama munches the thorny plant. Munch, munch!
How? Camels have big, tough lips.
Look closely. The top lip is split in two!
One half, two halves. Count them with me!
Each half can move on its own. Wiggle, wiggle!
Can you wiggle your lips? Wiggle, wiggle!
The lips are tough, but bendy. They pick at the little leaves.
Inside the mouth, there are lots of little bumps.
Count some bumps with me. One, two, three, four!
The bumps are hard, like your fingernails.
Tap your fingernails. Tap, tap! So hard!
The bumps help push the food down, to the tummy.
Every little bump points the same way. Down, down, down!
Where do the bumps push the food? Up to the nose, or down to the tummy?
Down to the tummy! So Mama can eat thorny plants.
Sandy tries a little thorny twig, too. Crunch!
Tough lips, and hard little bumps. Thorns, yum!
At the oasis, Sandy finds a different plant.
Sandy sniffs the leaves. They taste salty!
It is a salty plant, called saltbush.
Is saltbush salty, or sweet?
Can camels eat salty plants? Yes, or no?
Yes! Sandy nibbles the salty leaves. Munch!
Munch, munch. A salty snack for Sandy!
Salt is very important for camels.
Can you say saltbush? Salt, bush!
After lunch, Mama rests. But look, she is chewing again!
Camels bring their food back up, and chew it again!
Chew, chew, chew. Then chew some more!
Chew. Swallow. Then up it comes, to chew again!
Let's say it together. Camels chew it again!
Does a camel chew its food again? Yes, or no?
Let's chew like a camel. Chew, chew, chew!
And at the zoo, camels eat hay!
Mama munches the hay. Munch, munch!
Pretend to munch some hay. Munch, munch!
Grass, leaves, twigs, thorns, and salty plants!
Which camel lunch would you pick?
Time to remember what we learned!
What do camels eat? Plants, or candy?
Plants! Grass, leaves, and twigs.
Can camels eat thorny plants? Yes, or no?
Yes! With their big, tough lips.
How many halves does a camel's top lip have? One, or two?
Two! And each half wiggles on its own.
Thank you for learning with me, friends. See you at the zoo!
